A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FormulaCode study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of seven agent-model configurations on 108 FormulaCode-V tasks, including speedups, human-relative advantages, correctness failures, and trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds multiple-comparison, alternative-metric, and patch-similarity analyses.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix A.6 reports incorporating Holm-Bonferroni correction as an additional task-inclusion filter, refining the benchmark-construction procedure. The extraction prompts, environment-synthesis procedure, and evaluated agent algorithms otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover scientific-Python repository optimization and evaluate the same 108-task FormulaCode-V subset. The added analyses reuse this coverage. Removing 35 tasks under corrected filtering concerns selection within the existing corpus, rather than introducing a different domain or task scenario.

E2.justification: Both evaluate four models with Terminus 2 and three with OpenHands, retaining the expert reference. SWE-Perf is added to the related-work benchmark-properties table; it is not a newly evaluated experimental baseline.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 changes the central advantage aggregation from a difference of geometric-mean speedups to a geometric mean of per-workload differences. v3 also introduces corrected task filtering, log-space reranking, and patch-distance analysis stratified at absolute advantage 0.05. These are substantive reported scoring and analysis changes; retained leaderboard values do not establish that agent evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validity checks: Holm-corrected filtering tests task-selection robustness (A.6), linear-versus-log-space rankings test metric sensitivity (B.6, Table 15), and patch similarity tests memorization beyond temporal-cutoff analysis (B.7, Table 20). Existing hierarchy, popularity, tool-use, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 first specifies ASV's 2-40 adaptive measurements per workload and adds within-task Holm-Bonferroni correction. The existing Mann-Whitney threshold of p < 0.002 and fallback nonoverlapping 99% confidence intervals remain. This refines statistical validation and discloses repetition information without establishing increased agent-run counts.

E6.justification: New results include unchanged OpenHands Ranked Pairs ordering under LogAdv, patch edit distances of 0.94-0.98, and removal of 35 of 957 tasks under corrected filtering with no FormulaCode-V tasks affected. The correctness-rejection rate is corrected from 52.43% to approximately 48.5%, consistent with the retained counts. Main leaderboard values remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The revised advantage definition in Section 2.1 is mathematically nonequivalent to v2's difference of aggregated speedups. v3 does not explain how its geometric mean handles potentially negative per-workload advantages. Appendix B.6 additionally introduces LogAdv and a first-order Taylor argument relating it to linear advantage. These alter central mathematical definitions and reasoning, rather than notation alone.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim that agents make inferior performance-cost tradeoffs with a claim about inferior multi-workload performance tradeoffs, aligning the summary with Figure 5. The benchmark contribution, headline scale, and central claim that evaluated agents underperform experts remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific limitations concerning domain coverage, workload blind spots, subset generalization, and hardware dependence (Section 6 and A.9). Sections A.8 and B.6-B.8 expand difficulty and metric interpretations, routing and deployment implications, and the qualification that low patch similarity cannot exclude semantic contamination. This substantially broadens interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: New Tables 12-13 disclose pinned agent versions, decoding settings, context and iteration limits, time caps, and API specifications beyond v2's references to defaults. A.7 details subset selection and stratification. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without proving changed runs. The update day changes from the 31st to the 25th, while some snapshot-testing details, including skipping objects without defined equality, are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the assertion that He et al. do not test correctness with a fuller SWE-Perf comparison covering scale, unit-test timing, and contamination resistance, including a Table 6 row. Holm (1979) and Armstrong (2014) are added; the Cruz snapshot-testing and Droettboom ASV references are removed. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The dataset overview is rewritten and consolidated into a standalone Section 3 from material previously distributed across Section 2.2 and Appendix A. The appendices are reorganized around construction and experiments, with new limitations, metric-discussion, and implications subsections. This is substantial narrative restructuring, alongside terminology, cross-reference, and conference-header edits.

P2.justification: The dataset-statistics table moves from the appendix to the main text, and repository tables, task examples, and patch figures are extensively reordered. v3 adds Tables 12, 13, 15, and 20, extends the related-work table, and changes caption formatting and running headers. Most existing plots and case panels are retained, but the organization of displays changes substantially.

improvement.justification: The configuration tables, additional validity checks, corrected rejection rate, and explicit limitations address real documentation and validation gaps. However, Section 2.1 replaces v2's defined difference of aggregated speedups with a geometric mean of potentially negative advantages without explaining its mathematical treatment. The retained leaderboard and Appendix B.6 do not resolve which aggregation produced the results. These benefits coexist with new ambiguity in the central evaluation metric, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
